lines.say: Chapter six. The sentence.

Then, in the summer of twenty twenty-six, the case turned. About a week after Owens changed his plea, on July sixth, Lumumba pleaded guilty to a single conspiracy count. Banks did the same that afternoon.
lines.show: Then, in the summer of 2026, the case turned. About a week after Owens changed his plea, on July 6, Lumumba pleaded guilty to a single conspiracy count. Banks did the same that afternoon.

scene.sub: One conspiracy count · Banks pleads the same day · Owens about a week earlier

lines.say: In court, a federal prosecutor read the facts. Fifty thousand dollars in five ten-thousand-dollar checks, from F.B.I. sources posing as developers, received in Fort Lauderdale on April second, twenty twenty-four. The call to change the deadline. The deposit. The withdrawals for personal use. Lumumba told the judge he accepted those facts.
lines.show: In court, a federal prosecutor read the facts. $50,000 in five $10,000 checks, from FBI sources posing as developers, received in Fort Lauderdale on April 2, 2024. The call to change the deadline. The deposit. The withdrawals for personal use. Lumumba told the judge he accepted those facts.

scene.title: $50,000 · five $10,000 checks
scene.src: WLBT/WLOX (July 6, 2026) — plea hearing; U.S. Attorney's Office, S.D. Miss., press release (Nov 7, 2024)

lines.say: The conspiracy count carries up to five years in prison. In exchange for the pleas, the government agreed to drop the more substantive charges, according to the Mississippi Free Press.

scene.title: Conspiracy: not more than 5 years
scene.src: Notice of maximum penalties, Dkt. 3-1 (S.D. Miss. 3:24-cr-103); Mississippi Free Press (July 6, 2026) — plea hearing

lines.say: On November fifth, twenty twenty-six, Owens was sentenced first. Forty-one months in prison, and a one hundred thousand dollar fine. Banks got forty-five months and a fifteen thousand dollar fine.
lines.show: On November 5, 2026, Owens was sentenced first. 41 months in prison, and a $100,000 fine. Banks got 45 months and a $15,000 fine.

scene.title: Months in prison
scene.src: Mississippi Today (Nov 5, 2026) — Owens sentencing hearing; WLBT (Anthony Warren, Quentin Smith), Nov 20, 2026 — sentencing hearing; SuperTalk Mississippi (Nov 20, 2026)

lines.say: On November fifth, the day Owens was sentenced, Lumumba's own sentencing hearing began. The judge noted that the ask had been to move the date of the R.F.Q. The lead prosecutor, Dave Fulcher, called that a strawman set up by Lumumba's lawyers. The bribery scheme, he said, was: we need him involved.
lines.show: On November 5, the day Owens was sentenced, Lumumba's own sentencing hearing began. The judge noted that "the ask was to move the date of the RFQ." The lead prosecutor, Dave Fulcher, called that "a strawman that has been set up by Lumumba's counsel." The bribery scheme, he said, was: "We need him involved."

scene.q: That is a strawman that has been set up by Lumumba’s counsel. … The bribery scheme was, ‘We need him involved.’
scene.case: Dave Fulcher, federal prosecutor · Nov 5, 2026 · Lumumba presentence hearing
